pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 6.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: PLAY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are some of the issues authors write about?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the themes in a play or a section of a play

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the themes in a play or a section of a play
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the themes in a play or a section of a play. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play.
4. Show that you can: identify the themes in a play or a section of a play

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In groups discuss the themes in a play,
2. Role play some of the scenes in a play,
3. Creativity and imagination: It is enhanced as the learner participates in hot seats and relates themes to real life experiences.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are some of the issues authors write about?
2. How are literary texts different from factual ones?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the themes in a play or a section of a play

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
